## **Copper Monthly September 2011 No. 177** #### **Highlights** ##### **INSIDE THIS ISSUE** **Hot topics in Global Macro Economy** The global economy was in panic hit by the continuous negative news of the downgrading of United States sovereign credit rating and the dept crisis in Europe. After that, Standard & Poor’s lowered the expectation for the US economy growth in Q3 and Q4 from 1.9% to 1.8%. The company also lowered the country’s estimation economy growth in 2011 from 2.4% to 1.7%. Furthermore, Standard & Poor’s downgraded America’s economy growth in 2012 and 2013 to 2% and 2.1% respectively. The panicky investors still worried about the global depression and flocked to gold and the U.S. bond market despite U.S. government’s declaration of noting Standard & Poor’s estimation was based on incorrect data. Market is flooded with a lot of panic selling. But on the other hand, the U.S. bond market rebounded after the country’s sovereign credit rating was downgraded, which signaling the bond market was still the right place for the investors to avoid risk. Market participants were more concerned about the economy trend. ###### **_Highlights_** Hot topics in Global Macro Economy…….,.....1 ###### **_Copper Market Review_** Copper prices maintains a narrow range of shock…………………………………………,....2 Chinese refined copper imports hit second high in July………………………………….…...,......6 **_News_** China to increase nonferrous self-sufficiency rate by 2015……………..….……………,,..…..8 Daye Nonferrous's business results keep steady increase…………………………,,..,..….9 Zijin Mining's sales revenue gets a y-o-y 18% increase………….………..……..……………..10 Yunnan Copper to sell shares of Lanping Yunkuang….…………...………………..……..13 ##### **Statistics** Chinese Refined Copper Output by Region in July 2011…………………….……...….…….…14 Chinese Imports and Exports of Cu Products in July 2011………….…………..…………….......14 **_Market Data_** .…..……..……….…..….…........23 HSBC announced the preview of China’s manufacturing PMI on Aug. 23 that the index was Website: www.antaike.com 1 Copper Monthly No. 177 49.8 in August, still lower than 50, which means Chinese manufacturing still ran at a relatively slow-down status, only a little cooling down from the previous months. HSBC further noted that the China’s PMI was comparatively inactive in the past few months, but the company still estimated China's annual industrial output growth at 12-13%, GDP growth at 9%, encouraging the market. Overall, the recent global financial and commodity markets panic, forcing China to make fine-tuning on the monetary policy under the condition of pr

udent macro management. On the one hand, this will affect China's exports; on the other hand it will affect China's foreign exchange reserves, in turn leading to further reducing on the investment enthusiasm. Therefore, the government’s control on the monetary policy may be a little modest slowdown. If the concerns about world economic growth continue to spread and the decline in domestic economic growth faster than expected, the policy will be very possible to become tight ahead of schedule. 

#### **Copper Market Commentary** 

###### **Copper prices maintains a narrow range of shock** 

Copper for three month delivery on LME opened at US$9,886/t on Aug.1, and closed at US$9, 160/t on Aug. 30, touching a high of US$9,680/t on Aug.2 and a low of US$8,595/t on Aug.10. 

Due to worries for US and European economies, copper prices on the LME declined in early August, after a rise for five consecutive weeks. Ben Bernanke, the chairman of the Federal Reserve, gave a speech on August 26, named “The Near- and Longer-Term Prospects for the U.S. Economy”. Bernanke didn’t hint or implied of any further quantitative easing plan, but would take measures to boost economic development. Speech of Bernanke has led to growing optimism about the world economy. Copper price for three month delivery on LME opened at US$9,033/t and closed at US$9,075/t on Aug. 26, up US$45/t compared with US$9,030/t on Aug. 25. 

Copper for three month delivery on SHFE opened at 73,100yuan/t on Aug.1, and closed at 68,250yuan/t on Aug. 30, touching a high of 73,440yuan/t on Aug.1 and a low of 65,960yuan/t on Aug.9. 

Domestic copper prices followed the trend of copper prices on LME, but with lower growth rate. Currently, with the coming of copper consumption in the off-season, together with financial pressures and consumption restriction in downstream enterprises, bargain buy to fill stocks is likely to be limited and turnover is expected to be low. In addition, copper inventory has a certain decline recently, from 118,200t on Aug. 5 to 102,258t on Aug. 26, which is favorable for market expectation, but only small driver due to the bigger uncertain economic environment. 

The latest SHFE/LME arbitrage is favorable for imports. China imported 194.28kt refined copper, up by 8.70% m-o-m, a month-on- month increase for two consecutive months in 2011. It is expected refined copper import will rise to above 200kt in August. 

Investors are optimistic about copper market, which will support copper price uptrend. Copper prices decline is less likely to decline, but no sharp rise in 2011.

###### **Chinese refined copper output slightly down in July** 

Data released by China Nonferrous Metals Industry Association (CNIA) showed refined copper production was 451.11kt

in July, slightly down by 1% m-o-m or up by 16% y-o-y. The accumulative output from January to July was 2.97Mt, up by 13% y-o-y. According to statistics from Antaike, during Jan. to Jul., output of 12 Chinese main refined copper producers produced 2.23Mt, up by 12.56% y-o-y. That’s to say, larger enterprises had been expanding production, but some enterprises engaging in recycling copper with less competitiveness had to choose production reduction or shut down. As coming of copper consumption off-season, Chinese refined copper output was certainly affected. For the future, refined copper output will maintain at a high level. 

During January to July, accumulative refined copper output in Jiangxi, Shandong, Anhui, Gansu, Yunnan as the top 5 main regions for refined copper production increased by 7%, 5%, 1%, 16%, 16% year on year respectively, which contributed to the year-on-year growth. Although, the output of refined copper in July was lower than that in June, a 9% m-o-m increase of refined copper import will add supply of refined copper. 

Copper semis production reached 890.95kt in July, down by 9% m-o-m or up by 3% y-o-y. The accumulative output from January to July was 5.67Mt, up by 17% y-o-y. During January to July, accumulative output in Zhejiang, Jiangxi, Jiangsu, Anhui, Guangdong, etc. top 5 copper semis production provinces increased by 1%, 15%, 5%, 38%, and 32% year on year. 

Copper-in-concentrate production was 107.61kt in July, down by 7% m-o-m or up 16% y-o-y. The accumulative output from January to July was 699.14kt, up by 12% y-o-y. Analysis of data showed that copper-in-concentrate production of Jiangxi, Yunnan, Inner Mongolia, Anhui, xinjiang, etc. as China’s top 5 regions for copper-in-concentrate production, increased by 21%, 11%, 0.03%, 9% and 23% during January to July. It is expected that high copper prices will further promote enthusiasm for production of domestic mine enterprises, when import of copper concentrate appeared decline in July.

###### **Copper consumption** 

According to the latest statistics from National Bureau of Statistics of China (NBS), major domestic copper-using products output in Jan-July increased year on year by two digits, except autos, household ice-box and telecommunication cable. While, with the coming of copper consumption off-season and increasing pressure on capital surface, the month-on-month figures in July showed that most of domestic copper-using products output appears negative, except household refrigerator and transformer. 

According to the statistics from China Electricity Council, total investment in electric power reached 333.0 bln yuan during January to July, up by 6.8% y-o-y. Of which investment in power source and power grid was 176.8 bln yuan and 156.2 bln yuan, up by 6.0% and 7.8% y-o-y respectively. Of investment in power source, investment in hydropo

wer and nuclear power increased by 30.7% and 27.4% y-o-y; investment in thermal power and wind power decreased by 10.2% and 7.8% y-o-y. The year-on-year decline of investment in wind power appeared since May 2011. According to China Electricity Council statistics, growth rate of power consumption slows down in July. The cumulative total power consumption in January and July was 2686.9 TWh, up by 12.15% y-o-y, 8.10 percentage points lower than the same period of 2010. Power consumption in July was 434.9 TWh, up by 11.81% y-o-y, 2.13 percentage points lower than the same period of 2010. The power consumption for the primary industry was 59.1 TWh, increased by 5.10% y-o-y. The secondary industry consumed 2025.3 TWh, with a year-on-year increase of 11.94%. The tertiary industry had a power consumption of 285.3 TWh, up by 15.46% y-o-y. The power consumption for urban and rural residents reached 317.2 TWh, increased by 12.03% y-o-y. The cumulative average utilization time of generation equipment in China was 2,778 hours in January and July, increased by 56 hours compared with the same period of last year. The average utilization time for hydropower equipment was 1,774 hours, down 83 hours compared with last year. The time for coal-fired power equipment was 3,085 hours, increased by 119 hours compared with last year. The newly added power energy capacity that has been put into operation in China was 41.23 GW in Jan. and Jul., including 7.69 GW of hydropower, 27.74 GW of coal-fired power and 5.63 GW of wind power. **Ending using** **products output of copper industry in Jan.-Jul. 2011** |**Products**|**Unit**|**2009**

Production is adjusted by Antaike;_ ###### **Chinese refined copper imports hit second high in July** Data released by China Customs showed China’s refined copper imports rose to 194.28kt in July, hitting a second high in 2011 after the 245.62kt in January. The refined copper imports in July increased by 9% m-o-m but down 14% y-o-y. The latest SHFE/LME arbitrage is favorable for imports. It is expected refined copper import will rise to above 200kt in August. The imports of copper concentrate declined to 452.11kt in July, down 24% compared with 593.12kt in the previous month. Currently, domestic mine copper output kept at a relative high level. Although, self-produced copper concentrate increased, supply shortage of copper concentrate caused by import decline still existed. Import decline was mainly because of copper consumption off-season in July and lower spot TC/RCs during that period. Market outlook remains to be seen, but low level of copper concentrate is expected to be changed for the future. As to the copper scraps, the import volume climbed up further to 432.32kt in July, also hitting a new high this year. The monthly growth rate of Chinese copper scraps imports was 3%. The reasons for the increase are as follows: firstly, partial importers were optimistic for the future copper prices and imported large numbers of copper scraps during May to June, which caused increase of commodities in port in July; secondly, importers were more willing to buy brass and scrap motor with smaller prices fluctuation, due to larger prices fluctuation of refined copper in June and July. The current copper scraps supply is still tight. Copper scrap import will not decline for the future.
